input.quote: 6.1 Except as provided in Section 6.2, during the term of this Agreement, the Company shall not participate in any project similar to the Site on the Internet with respect to Deerskin Products or products substantially similar to Deerskin Products (including, without limitation, the products of Wilson's House of Leather, Excelled and companies similar to Wilson's House of Leather and Excelled) and HDI shall have the exclusive right to use of the "Deerskin" brand for a self-contained web site for the offering of Deerskin Products directly to the consumer on the Internet.
input.rationale: Section 6.1 imposes a non-compete and field-of-use restriction on us: we may not participate in any project similar to the Site with respect to Deerskin Products or any "products substantially similar" (an open-ended category expressly extending to "companies similar to" named competitors), and HDI additionally takes an exclusive right over our own "Deerskin" brand for direct-to-consumer Internet sales. This fails the fallback on several material terms: the scope is not a single named competing product; the only carve-out (Section 6.2) is limited to closeout "Deerskin" merchandise, with no carve-out for our internal development or for acquisitions; and although the covenant runs "during the term of this Agreement", the term auto-renews annually under Section 4.1, so the restriction is not capped at 12 months. Because HDI's retained exclusive right would still prevent us from using or licensing our own brand, we have taken the preferred position and removed both the Company covenant and the exclusivity in Section 6.1, leaving Section 6.2 and HDI's own restriction in Section 6.3 untouched.

proposal.summary: Remove the Company non-compete and HDI's exclusive "Deerskin" brand right in Section 6.1
proposal.comment: [Playbook] We cannot accept a restriction on the products we offer or the sites we operate, so we have removed the Company's covenant in Section 6.1 and HDI's exclusive right over our own "Deerskin" brand. If HDI needs protection, we could discuss a narrow restriction limited to a named competing product, during the term only and capped at 12 months, with carve-outs for our internal development and acquisitions.
